points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 莱布尼茨出生于莱比锡的一个书香门第，父亲是哲学教授。他自幼展现出非凡的智力，六岁便能阅读拉丁文，八岁开始学习希腊文。12岁时进入莱比锡大学预科学校，15岁（1661年）进入莱比锡大学学习哲学、法律和数学。在此期间，他广泛阅读亚里士多德、笛卡尔等哲学家的著作，并开始发展自己的哲学思想。这段早期教育为他后来的多领域成就奠定了坚实基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Leipzig to a scholarly family, Leibniz showed exceptional intellectual abilities from a young age, reading Latin at six and Greek at eight. At 12, he entered the University of Leipzig preparatory school, and at 15 (1661), he enrolled at the university to study philosophy, law, and mathematics. During this period, he extensively read works by Aristotle, Descartes, and other philosophers, beginning to develop his own philosophical ideas. This early education laid the solid foundation for his later achievements in multiple fields.

points.title: 外交生涯开端
points.description: 1667年，莱布尼茨进入美因茨选帝侯的宫廷，开始其外交生涯。他被委派一项重要任务：说服法国国王路易十四将军队从德意志地区撤出，转而进攻埃及。虽然这一计划未被采纳，但莱布尼茨在此期间发展出了一套关于国际关系的理论。1670年，他发表了《论选帝侯的政治改革》，提出了统一德意志各邦国的方案。这段外交经历使莱布尼茨接触到欧洲政治的核心，也促使他思考如何通过理性方法解决政治问题。
points.descriptionEn: In 1667, Leibniz entered the court of the Elector of Mainz, beginning his diplomatic career. He was entrusted with a crucial mission: to persuade Louis XIV of France to withdraw his troops from German territories and instead attack Egypt. Although this plan was not adopted, Leibniz developed a theory of international relations during this period. In 1670, he published 'Political Reform of the Electorate,' proposing a plan to unify the German states. This diplomatic experience exposed Leibniz to the core of European politics and prompted him to reflect on how to solve political problems through rational methods.

points.title: 巴黎学术探索
points.description: 1672年，莱布尼茨作为外交使节前往巴黎，在此停留了四年。这段时期是他学术生涯的黄金时期。他结识了当时欧洲最杰出的学者，包括惠更斯、马勒伯朗士等。在惠更斯的指导下，莱布尼茨深入研究数学，发明了微积分（与牛顿独立发展）。他还开始系统研究哲学，形成了自己的形而上学体系。1675年，他发明了第一台能进行乘除运算的计算器。巴黎的学术氛围极大地激发了莱布尼茨的创造力，使他能够在多个领域同时取得突破性进展。
points.descriptionEn: In 1672, Leibniz traveled to Paris as a diplomatic envoy, staying for four years. This period was the golden age of his academic career. He met the most distinguished scholars in Europe, including Huygens and Malebranche. Under Huygens' guidance, Leibniz deeply studied mathematics and independently developed calculus (alongside Newton). He also began systematically studying philosophy, forming his own metaphysical system. In 1675, he invented the first calculator capable of performing multiplication and division. Paris's academic atmosphere greatly stimulated Leibniz's creativity, enabling him to make breakthroughs in multiple fields simultaneously.

points.title: 汉诺威宫廷服务
points.description: 1676年，莱布尼茨接受汉诺威公爵的邀请，成为宫廷顾问和图书馆馆长，在此度过了余生。他负责管理公爵图书馆，并参与历史研究项目，编纂了不伦瑞克家族史。1700年，他促成柏林科学院的成立，并担任首任院长。在汉诺威期间，莱布尼茨继续在哲学、数学、科学、历史等多个领域工作，发表了大量著作。他试图调和天主教与新教之间的分歧，并提出了建立世界通用语言的构想。尽管在汉诺威的职位相对次要，但莱布尼茨在此完成了他最重要的哲学著作《单子论》和《神义论》。
points.descriptionEn: In 1676, Leibniz accepted an invitation from the Duke of Hanover to become a court advisor and librarian, serving there for the rest of his life. He managed the ducal library and participated in historical research projects, compiling the history of the Brunswick family. In 1700, he facilitated the establishment of the Berlin Academy of Sciences and served as its first president. During his time in Hanover, Leibniz continued to work in multiple fields including philosophy, mathematics, science, and history, publishing numerous works. He attempted to reconcile Catholicism and Protestantism and proposed the creation of a universal world language. Although his position in Hanover was relatively minor, Leibniz completed his most important philosophical works, 'Monadology' and 'Theodicy,' during this period.

points.title: 学术期刊创办
points.description: 1682年，莱布尼茨与同事奥托·门克共同创办了学术期刊《学术纪事》(Acta Eruditorum)，这是德语地区最早的学术期刊之一。该期刊迅速成为欧洲最重要的学术交流平台之一，发表了许多重要科学发现和理论。莱布尼茨利用这一平台发表了自己的数学和哲学著作，包括微积分的早期论文。通过《学术纪事》，莱布尼茨建立了与欧洲各地学者的广泛联系，促进了知识的传播和交流。这一期刊的创办体现了莱布尼茨对科学传播和学术交流的重视，也反映了他希望通过理性方法推动人类进步的信念。
points.descriptionEn: In 1682, Leibniz co-founded the academic journal 'Acta Eruditorum' with his colleague Otto Mencke, one of the earliest academic journals in the German-speaking world. The journal quickly became one of the most important platforms for academic exchange in Europe, publishing many important scientific discoveries and theories. Leibniz used this platform to publish his mathematical and philosophical works, including early papers on calculus. Through 'Acta Eruditorum,' Leibniz established extensive connections with scholars across Europe, promoting the dissemination and exchange of knowledge. The founding of this journal reflected Leibniz's emphasis on scientific communication and academic exchange, as well as his belief in advancing human progress through rational methods.

points.title: 晚年哲学体系完善
points.description: 1714年，莱布尼茨移居柏林，担任普鲁士王后索菲夏洛特的政治顾问。在此期间，他完成了自己哲学体系的代表作《单子论》，系统阐述了他的形而上学思想。他提出了'单子'理论，认为宇宙由无数'单子'构成，每个单子都是独立的精神实体，通过'前定和谐'相互协调。他还完成了《神义论》，试图证明上帝存在的合理性。在柏林的最后两年，莱布尼茨致力于将他的哲学思想系统化，并试图说服欧洲君主支持他的科学和哲学计划。尽管他的许多宏大构想未能实现，但这一时期的思想成果对后世哲学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1714, Leibniz moved to Berlin to serve as a political advisor to Queen Sophie Charlotte of Prussia. During this period, he completed his philosophical masterpiece 'Monadology,' systematically expounding his metaphysical thoughts. He proposed his theory of 'monads,' suggesting that the universe consists of innumerable 'monads,' each an independent spiritual entity, coordinated through 'pre-established harmony.' He also completed 'Theodicy,' attempting to demonstrate the rationality of God's existence. In his final two years in Berlin, Leibniz devoted himself to systematizing his philosophical ideas and trying to persuade European monarchs to support his scientific and philosophical plans. Although many of his grand visions were not realized, the intellectual achievements of this period had a profound impact on later philosophy.

supporter.zh: 莱布尼茨是人类历史上最博学的天才之一，他的贡献跨越哲学、数学、科学、历史、外交等多个领域。他独立发明了微积分，创立了单子论哲学体系，推动了科学方法的发展，并促进了欧洲学术交流。莱布尼茨的思想体现了理性主义和乐观主义精神，他认为我们生活于'所有可能世界中最好的世界'。他的跨学科思维和追求普遍知识的热情，使他成为启蒙运动的重要先驱，对后世科学发展产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Leibniz was one of the most learned geniuses in human history, whose contributions spanned philosophy, mathematics, science, history, and diplomacy. He independently invented calculus, created the monadological philosophical system, advanced scientific methodology, and promoted academic exchange across Europe. Leibniz's thoughts embodied rationalist and optimistic spirit, as he believed we live in 'the best of all possible worlds.' His interdisciplinary thinking and passion for universal knowledge made him an important precursor to the Enlightenment, exerting profound influence on the development of modern science.

critic.zh: 批评者认为莱布尼茨的思想体系过于抽象和复杂，难以验证和应用。他的'前定和谐'理论被指责为回避了现实世界中的矛盾和冲突。在科学方法上，他与牛顿的微积分之争反映了其理论不够严谨。此外，莱布尼茨作为宫廷顾问的实际政治影响力有限，他的许多宏伟计划未能实现。他的乐观主义哲学也被批评为忽视了现实世界中的苦难和不公。一些现代哲学家认为他的形而上学体系过于依赖神学预设，缺乏坚实的经验基础。
critic.en: Critics argue that Leibniz's philosophical system is overly abstract and complex, difficult to verify and apply. His 'pre-established harmony' theory has been accused of avoiding contradictions and conflicts in the real world. In scientific methodology, his dispute with Newton over calculus reflected theoretical shortcomings. Additionally, Leibniz's actual political influence as a court advisor was limited, and many of his grand plans remained unfulfilled. His optimistic philosophy has also been criticized for ignoring suffering and injustice in the real world. Some modern philosophers argue that his metaphysical system relies too heavily on theological presuppositions and lacks a solid empirical foundation.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，莱布尼茨被视为17-18世纪欧洲知识转型的关键人物，连接了文艺复兴与启蒙运动。他既是理性主义的代表，又保留了神学传统，体现了早期现代思想的复杂性。在流行文化中，莱布尼茨常被描绘为'最后一位通才'，象征着知识探索的黄金时代。他与牛顿的微积分之争已成为科学史上的经典案例，展示了天才竞争的创造性张力。莱布尼茨的符号逻辑思想虽未被同时代充分重视，但被视为现代数理逻辑和计算机科学的先驱，影响远超其时代。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Leibniz is regarded as a pivotal figure in the European intellectual transformation of the 17th-18th centuries, bridging the Renaissance and Enlightenment. He represents both rationalism and theological tradition, embodying the complexity of early modern thought. In popular culture, Leibniz is often depicted as 'the last universal genius,' symbolizing the golden age of intellectual exploration. His calculus dispute with Newton has become a classic case in the history of science, demonstrating the creative tension between geniuses. Although his symbolic logic was not fully appreciated in his time, Leibniz is now recognized as a precursor to modern mathematical logic and computer science, with influence far beyond his era.

self.zh: 我们生活于所有可能世界中最好的世界。
self.en: We live in the best of all possible worlds.

others.zh: 莱布尼茨是如此罕见的天才，他在如此多的领域都达到了第一流的水平，以至于我们几乎可以称他为超人的。
others.en: Leibniz was such a rare genius that he reached the first rank in so many fields that we can almost call him superhuman.
